coupled_branches.interpretation: K=4 wins one-axis K comparisons, but coordinated length/K changes expose short/low-K and long/high-K competitive ridges

definition.interpretation: observed topology at sampled resolution; does not prove that unsampled zones are absent

ridge_closure.interpretation: closure is local to measured inner/outward K evidence; a winning K=1 or K=7 point is a registered-domain boundary seed, not a proven unconstrained optimum

coupled_branch_seeds.interpretation: K=4 wins one-axis K comparisons, but coordinated length/K changes expose short/low-K and long/high-K competitive ridges

domain.geometry: axisymmetric round-mouth, zero extension, 6 degree throat

rules.action: start each axis at the tabulated/bilinearly interpolated reference OSSE length
start K at 4; do not infer that larger K is better
start N at 8; N=4 is the first alternate and N=16 is not an initial candidate
after a material K/N change, preserve the coverage-level S seed first, then recheck at least ±10% length because the preferred length interacts with K/N
use the median S of measured cell winners as a physical ridge seed when K or N changes
carry the short/low-K, center, and long/high-K branches as distinct starts; do not optimize length or K alone
retain observed competitive components outside the benchmark component as alternate search starts
use the per-cell final measured seed; where K=1 or K=7 wins, label it a registered-domain boundary rather than an unconstrained optimum
for unequal H/V targets, combine independent axis seed lengths using mouth-width/height score weights
optionally shorten only the axis with the shorter seed length by using cylindrical sag equal to the axis-length difference
rules.status: exact at principal mouth edges in current geometry; acoustic benefit unvalidated

status: measured seed rules; not a score predictor
